artworks.title: Plate Number 609. "Lizzie M." trotting, harnessed to sulky
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of frames depicting a horse in motion. The image is a composite of multiple individual frames arranged in rows, showing a horse pulling a carriage with large wheels across a sequence. Each frame captures a slightly different moment in the horse's stride, illustrating the movement of the horse and the carriage over time. The photographs are in black and white, emphasizing the contrast between the horse and the lighter background. The repeated visuals create a narrative of motion, drawing attention to the mechanics of the horse's gait and the rhythmic progression of the carriage's wheels.

artworks.title: Plate Number 610. "Katydid" trotting, harnessed to sulky
artworks.description: This is a series of sequential images depicting a horse pulling a cart in motion. The images show the horse's trotting gait from different angles, illustrating various leg positions as the horse moves. The top row offers a side view while the bottom row provides a front view. The frames are numbered to show the progression of movement systematically. The horse is set against a gridded background, suggesting a scientific analysis of its gait.

artworks.title: Plate Number 611. "Katydid" trotting, harnessed to sulky
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse pulling a cart in sequential movement. The image is a series of black and white photographs capturing a horse in motion as it pulls a two-wheeled cart. Each frame shows a slightly different phase of the horse's gait. The grid-like background suggests a scientific study of motion commonly associated with early photographic motion studies. The images are presented in a grid format, showing two different perspectives of the same action — a side view and a rear view.

artworks.title: Plate Number 612. "Dercum" trotting, harnessed to sulky
artworks.description: This is a series of frames depicting a horse pulling a cart from various angles. The frames capture the sequential movements of the horse, showing its legs, body, and the cart's wheels in detail. The top row displays the side view, while the bottom row shows a front view. The frames focus on the horse's movement, resembling studies of animal locomotion in early photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 613. "Nellie Rose" trotting, harnessed to sulky
artworks.description: This is a series of sequential frames of a horse pulling a sulky. The frames depict the horse's movement in a trot, showing different positions of its legs and body. The wheels of the sulky are also shown spinning as the horse moves. The series of images captures the dynamic motion of the horse and the vehicle, resembling early motion studies like those by Eadweard Muybridge.

artworks.title: Plate Number 614. "Flode Holden" trotting, harnessed to sulky, breaking into a gallop
artworks.description: This is a series of images showing a horse pulling a cart. The grid arrangement shows sequential shots of the horse's movement and the cart's wheels. The frames capture different positions of the horse's legs and the cart's wheels as they move. The composition experiments with motion and photography by displaying various moments in time in a linear layout.

artworks.title: Plate Number 615. "Hansel" cantering, bareback
artworks.description: The image shows a series of black and white photographs arranged in a grid pattern, depicting a human figure riding a horse. The photos capture different stages of a trot, with the rider seated upright on the horse's back. The background is plain with a grid-like pattern, and the ground appears flat. The sequence illustrates the motion of the horse and rider, focusing on the horse's legs in various stages of the trot.

artworks.title: Plate Number 616. "Daisy" cantering, saddled
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion. The image shows a series of sequential frames laid out in a grid format, capturing the different stages of a horse's trot. In each frame, the position of the horse's legs changes, depicting the movement and rhythmic gait characteristic of the animal. The horse remains centered in each panel, demonstrating the nuances of its stride as it progresses from left to right across the sequence. The backdrop is plain, likely to emphasize the motion study, allowing for a clear focus on the horse's movement against the neutral background.

artworks.title: Plate Number 617. "Clinton" cantering, bareback; rider nude
artworks.description: The image consists of multiple frames showing a nude male figure riding a white horse. The man sits upright on the horse, holding the reins, with his entire body visible. The horse is in motion, walking or trotting, and is consistently white with a prominent mane and tail. The background is dark, and the frames are arranged in a grid format showcasing the progression of the horse and rider along a straight path.

artworks.title: Plate Number 618. "Middleton" cantering, saddled
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a motion study involving a horse and rider. The full composition consists of sequential images arranged in a grid format, capturing the movement of a horse during different stages of a gallop. The top two rows display side-profile shots of the horse and rider as they progress through the stages of galloping. The lower row presents a series of front-facing images, focusing on the horse’s head and legs. This sequence was likely captured to analyze the biomechanical aspects of equestrian movement. Each photograph in the sequence is numbered.

artworks.title: Plate Number 619. "Middleton" cantering, saddled
artworks.description: This is a sequence of black and white images showing different angles of a horse in motion. The top row displays side profiles of the horse at various stages, showcasing trotting movements. The bottom row features rear perspectives of the horse in motion. Each image is numbered to signify the progression of movement. The series offers a detailed examination of equine motion, akin to early photographic studies focusing on analyzing movement through a set of images.

artworks.title: Plate Number 620. "Annie G." cantering, saddled
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion. The image shows a sequential series of smaller frames arranged in two rows, each capturing a different stage of a horse's movement. The top row primarily shows side profiles of the horse as it gallops, highlighting the various positions of the legs, body, and head in motion. The lower row provides rear views, demonstrating the dynamics and rhythm of the gallop from behind.

artworks.title: Plate Number 621. "Annie G." cantering, saddled
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a horse in motion captured in sequential frames. The image features two horizontal rows of photographs capturing the movement of a galloping horse from different angles. The top row shows side views, while the bottom row displays front views of the horse in motion. Each frame in the sequence documents the incremental motion of the horse during the gallop.

artworks.title: Plate Number 622. "Smith" cantering, saddled; rider nude
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of images of a horse in mid-gallop. The image features multiple sequential frames laid out in a grid format, showing the movement of a horse as it runs from left to right in the upper rows, and the rear view of the horse moving toward the observer in the bottom row. The sequence captures different phases of the horse's stride, revealing the dynamics of its motion and the movement of the tail and legs. The images are in black and white, with a focus on the natural action of the horse's gait. The backdrop of each frame is neutral, allowing for detailed observation of the horse's movement across the series.

artworks.title: Plate Number 623. "Smith" cantering, bareback; rider nude

Each frame shows the gradual progression of the horse's gait, first from a side view capturing the right profile of the horse and then from a rear view. The background is plain and consistent, serving as a neutral backdrop to emphasize the motion and anatomy of the horse. The use of sequential images in this manner suggests an interest in the scientific study of motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 624. "Daisy" galloping, saddled

The frames are arranged in two rows, each showing the horse at slightly different positions and poses, illustrating the phases of its stride. The background is a simple, light-colored wall. The horse's mane and tail are captured mid-flow, and the dynamics of muscle movement and limb positioning are clearly visible, demonstrating the use of early motion photography to study animal locomotion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 625. "Bouquet" galloping

The background is simple and minimal, focusing on the detailed anatomy and dynamic motion of the horse. The photograph emphasizes the mechanics of equine locomotion and the interaction between the rider and the horse.

artworks.title: Plate Number 626. "Annie G." galloping

Each photo shows the horse in mid-stride, illustrating the successive movements of its gallop from left to right. The background is plain, emphasizing the nuanced shifts in the position of the horse's legs and body in each frame.

artworks.title: Plate Number 627. "Annie G." galloping
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequence of a horse galloping. The series of frames capture different positions of the horse in motion, from stride to stride. The black and white images focus on the horse's motion without distractions of color or additional elements.

artworks.title: Plate Number 628. "Daisy" galloping
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion captured in a series of sequential shots. Each frame captures a specific moment in time, illustrating the movement and form of the horse as it progresses through its stride. The black and white photograph highlights contrast, allowing the muscular dynamics of the horse and the movement to be clearly observed against the lighter background. This series shows the elegance and power of the horse's movement, frozen in distinct sequential moments.

artworks.title: Plate Number 629. "Hansel" galloping, bareback

The background appears plain and consistent across the frames, emphasizing the horse's movements. The sequence captures a sense of motion and continuity, serving as a visual study of the horse's dynamic movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 630. "Pandora" galloping, saddled

The upper row of images presents a frontal perspective, where the horse is moving towards the viewer, while the lower row shows a rear view, illustrating the continuation of the motion away from the viewer. The images are in black and white.

artworks.title: Plate Number 631. "Bouquet" galloping, saddled

Each frame is marked with a number, suggesting a scientific or analytical approach to the study of motion. The backdrop is neutral, focusing attention on the horse's dynamic movement. The layout resembles the style of Eadweard Muybridge, known for his work in animal locomotion photography.
